```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Try a database with real browser sign-in before configuring your own server.
The package includes Docker files, a Shiny app, demo accounts and sample data.
You need R with shinyOAuthDB installed and Docker running with Linux containers
and Compose v2. You can use Windows, macOS or Linux.

## Start a demo

```{r launch}
shinyOAuthDB::oauth_db_demo()             # PostgreSQL 18
```

Wait for the launcher to print the app address, then open
`http://localhost:18100`. The first build downloads images and R packages;
PostgreSQL also compiles its native OAuth libraries. Builds need internet
access and several GB of disk space. Later starts reuse Docker's cache.

| Account | Password | Rows shown by the app |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `alice` | `alice-fixture-password` | `alice-visible-1`, `alice-visible-2` |
| `bob` | `bob-fixture-password` | `bob-visible-1`, `bob-visible-2` |

Click **Sign in** and use either account. In the default PostgreSQL demo,
signing in with the other account changes the rows you can see. The database
applies the restriction; the app sends the same query for both people.

Keycloak, the open-source sign-in server, uses `https://localhost:18443`.
Your browser may ask you to accept its generated local test certificate.
The app trusts this demo's CA; the launcher doesn't change your
computer's certificate store.

## Run and edit Shiny in local R

The default `app = "docker"` runs everything in containers, including R and
the database driver. Choose `app = "local"` to run the app in an R process
on your computer, using your installed R packages. Docker still runs the
database, Keycloak and the services needed by that database.

PostgREST is an easy first example: it queries PostgreSQL over HTTPS, so
your local R installation doesn't need a database driver.

```{r local-app}
install.packages("callr")
shinyOAuthDB::oauth_db_demo("postgrest", app = "local")
```

The launcher prints the path to your editable `app.R`. Open it in your
editor, change the query or UI, save it and reload the browser. The local
Shiny process watches that file for changes. Sign in with the same Alice
and Bob accounts as above.

To open the file before starting the demo:

```{r edit-local-app}
path <- shinyOAuthDB::oauth_db_demo("postgrest", app = "local", action = "files")
file.edit(file.path(path, "local-app", "postgrest", "app.R"))
shinyOAuthDB::oauth_db_demo("postgrest", app = "local", path = path)
```

Your edits stay between runs. Local mode uses a separate default directory
from Docker mode. Use the same `app = "local"` and `path` when resuming or
stopping a local demo. **Stop demo** or an R interrupt stops the local app
and removes the Docker containers and data.

| Local app | What you need in local R |
| --- | --- |
| PostgREST, libSQL, CrateDB, OpenSearch | callr and jsonlite; no database driver |
| Trino | callr and RTrino 0.1.0 or later |
| DuckDB Quack | callr and a DuckDB 1.5.4 client matching the server; the launcher installs its Quack/httpfs extensions |
| StarRocks | callr, odbc and MySQL Connector/ODBC 9.2 or later with its OpenID Connect plugin |
| Native PostgreSQL | callr, Linux and shinyOAuthDB/RPostgres built against the same shared libpq 18 |

The launcher reports missing R packages before starting Docker. PostgreSQL's
native client cannot run in local R on Windows or macOS; use PostgREST there,
or keep the PostgreSQL app in Docker. For StarRocks, check `driver` and
`plugin_dir` in the copied app against your local MySQL ODBC installation.
You can set `OAUTHDB_DEMO_ODBC_DRIVER` before copying the app to supply a
registered driver name (required on Windows), or a library path on Unix.
For a separate plugin directory, set `OAUTHDB_DEMO_ODBC_PLUGINS` before
copying the app, or edit `plugin_dir` in the copied file.

Local mode requires Docker Compose 2.24.4 or later. It leaves port 18100
for local Shiny and publishes the selected database endpoint on
`localhost:19444`. The app uses the demo's generated CA, with certificate
verification enabled. Only its own R process trusts that CA; your R
session and system certificate store keep their existing settings.

## Choose another database

Run one demo at a time; they share the same browser ports.

| Command | What runs | Guide |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `oauth_db_demo("postgres")` | PostgreSQL 18 with native OAuth and row policies | [PostgreSQL](postgres.html) |
| `oauth_db_demo("postgrest")` | PostgreSQL and PostgREST with JWT role mapping | [PostgREST](postgrest.html) |
| `oauth_db_demo("trino")` | Trino, an in-memory catalog and row filters | [Trino](trino.html) |
| `oauth_db_demo("starrocks")` | StarRocks with JWT users and a filtered view | [StarRocks](starrocks.html) |
| `oauth_db_demo("duckdb")` | DuckDB Quack with JWT validation and read-only access | [DuckDB](duckdb.html) |
| `oauth_db_demo("libsql")` | libSQL with Ed25519-signed database tokens | [libSQL](libsql.html) |
| `oauth_db_demo("cratedb")` | CrateDB with JWT users and read-only table grants | [CrateDB](cratedb.html) |
| `oauth_db_demo("opensearch")` | OpenSearch Security with per-user document permissions | [OpenSearch](opensearch.html) |

DuckDB, libSQL and CrateDB give both accounts read-only access to the same
sample table, containing `shared-visible-1` and `shared-visible-2`. These
databases enforce their read-only policy on the server. OpenSearch gives
each person their own documents. These four apps show the signed-in
account and include **Try a write**, which the database should reject.

With `app = "docker"`, Docker supplies the R packages and drivers too.
StarRocks needs roughly 4 GB of Docker memory and uses amd64 images, so other architectures need
emulation. Trino and OpenSearch each need at least 2 GB for their database
container. DuckDB downloads a matching R client and Quack extensions. It
compiles the client from source if a Linux binary isn't available, which
takes longer.

Cloud platforms need real accounts and OAuth registrations; a local Docker
container cannot reproduce that setup. ClickHouse's custom-provider JWT
feature needs a qualifying Cloud service.

## How the extra token formats work

The additional demos use `realm-extended.json`, which registers separate
Shiny clients for the four databases. DuckDB validates Keycloak tokens with
`quack_oauth`; OpenSearch validates the provider's signing key and applies
document permissions. OpenSearch takes a signing-key snapshot at startup.

Self-hosted libSQL needs a specific database token format. Its demo client
uses Keycloak's Ed25519 signing key, `id=default` and `a=ro` claims, and no
access-token audience. A separate service client seeds the database with
write access; the Shiny app receives only read-only tokens. This is a
self-hosted libSQL demo, separate from Turso Cloud's external-provider setup.

CrateDB expects the token's issuer URL to return its signing keys directly.
Its demo includes a local HTTPS gateway that serves Keycloak's public keys
at that URL and forwards the usual sign-in endpoints to Keycloak. Tokens
stay unchanged; CrateDB checks their signatures and enforces user grants.
For another provider, follow its [token requirements](cratedb.html).

## Stop and clean up

Click **Stop demo** or interrupt the foreground R call. Cleanup removes
that demo's containers, network and database volumes. Docker images and
the copied configuration stay for the next run.

If R exits forcibly, restart R and stop the same database:

```{r stop}
shinyOAuthDB::oauth_db_demo("postgres", action = "stop")
# For the local app example:
shinyOAuthDB::oauth_db_demo("postgrest", app = "local", action = "stop")
```

Use the same `path` too if you chose a custom directory. The launcher prints
a complete recovery command before starting containers.

## Change the app or inspect the configuration

Copy the files without starting Docker:

```{r files}
path <- shinyOAuthDB::oauth_db_demo("postgres", action = "files")
file.edit(file.path(path, "postgres", "app.R"))
shinyOAuthDB::oauth_db_demo("postgres", path = path)
```

`compose.yml` defines Keycloak and the app; `compose.postgres.yml` adds
PostgreSQL. `realm.json` configures the original demos; `realm-extended.json`
adds clients and claims for DuckDB, libSQL, CrateDB and OpenSearch.
The backend subdirectory contains its app and database configuration.
Edits in this directory survive subsequent launches. Use a new empty `path`
after upgrading the package to obtain fresh templates.

These are disposable, local configurations with public passwords. For a
deployment, replace the accounts, secrets, certificates and hostnames,
then follow the database guide's OAuth setup instructions.

In Docker mode, the app images install pinned revisions of shinyOAuth and
shinyOAuthDB from GitHub, listed in `install.R`. They don't use your local R library.
Maintainers can update those revisions after testing a new package release.

## If the demo doesn't start

If Docker isn't found, install Docker Desktop or Docker Engine with Compose
v2, then restart R so it picks up your PATH. Start the Docker daemon and
select Linux containers. On a port conflict, stop the other local demo or
the program using ports 18100 and 18443 (and 19444 in local mode).

Read the Docker output for failed downloads, low disk space or memory
limits. Retry with the default `build = TRUE` after fixing the problem;
`build = FALSE` only works after images have built successfully.
An app that starts but can't sign in usually needs the browser's local
certificate exception. Keep `localhost` in the URL; `127.0.0.1` doesn't
match the registered callback.
